newsitem.title: USA: Sun's JavaSoft says fixes bug in Java.
newsitem.headline: Sun's JavaSoft says fixes bug in Java.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc.'s JavaSoft unit said Monday it has developed software to correct a bug in the latest version of Sun's popular Java development kit.

The bug, a flaw in the Java Development Kit that prevents it from working properly, was reported by University of Washington computer science researchers. The software, version 1.1.2 of the Java kit, was released earlier this month.
The impact of the flaw is expected to be limited since JavaSoft said it was not present on earlier releases of Java or on any version of the Netscape Communications Corp. or Microsoft Corp. browsers.
"There's already a fix and it's going out in the 1.1.3 release," a spokeswoman said, adding the upcoming release is due to be posted on the JavaSoft Web site later this week.

Sun said the flaw would allow a small programme known as an "applet" to search and locate information stored on a browser's address space. That could allow computer hackers to collect information from a user visiting a Web site where the hacker had installed the applet.

Java was introduced by Sun Microsystems two years ago to help software developers write programmes designed to work on virtually every major computer system, even though those systems are otherwise largely incompatible.
Java has been licensed by a wide variety of software systems companies, ranging from Microsoft to computer giant International Business Machines Corp.
The Java software is particularly popular for use on the Internet and on corporate networks that use Web technology known as intranets.
